football_evidence.question: Can New Mexico State win at the line of scrimmage?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 0.7 points.
supporting: When Sam Houston has the ball (big plays on the ground): Sam Houston’s offense turns 3.4% of its runs into explosive gains, and New Mexico State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 7.0% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Sam Houston has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Sam Houston’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 25.4% of its runs, and New Mexico State’s defense stops 21.8% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.3%).

When New Mexico State has the ball (big plays on the ground): New Mexico State’s offense turns 7.4% of its runs into explosive gains, and Sam Houston’s defense gives up explosive gains on 10.4% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Sam Houston has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Sam Houston’s offense has allowed a sack on 6.6% of its dropbacks, and New Mexico State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.5% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
contradicting: When New Mexico State has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): New Mexico State’s offense averages 6.5 yards per pass attempt, and Sam Houston’s defense allows 5.4 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).
In his last two games (New Mexico and Florida International), Hedden averaged 4.6 yards per attempt, against 8.2 in his three games before that.
In his last two games (Western Kentucky and Florida International), Damante averaged 5.2 yards per attempt, against 9.9 in his two games before that.

When New Mexico State has the ball (the red zone): New Mexico State’s offense succeeds on 21.6% of its red-zone plays, and Sam Houston’s defense allows success on 43.4% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
quarterbacks: Landyn Locke has completed 129 of 208 passes (62.0%) for 1,418 yards, 6.8 yards per attempt, 11 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in six games for Sam Houston, and has been sacked on 15 of 223 dropbacks.

Trey Hedden has completed 65 of 125 passes (52.0%) for 933 yards, 7.5 yards per attempt, 5 touchdowns and 6 interceptions in five games for New Mexico State, and has been sacked on 7 of 132 dropbacks.
Adam Damante has completed 44 of 71 passes (62.0%) for 477 yards, 6.7 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in four games for New Mexico State, and has been sacked on 4 of 75 dropbacks.
